s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing vascular tumor on the scalp
salient_findings: 8-mm red, firm, mobile nodule on the left temporal scalp
Irregular red lacunae with irregular vessels and absence of septa on dermoscopic evaluation
Well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor with ectatic thin-walled vessels and intravascular branching papillary structures on histopathology
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 40s
The patient has no significant medical history
The tumor is located on the left temporal scalp
The tumor is 8-mm in size
The tumor is red, firm, and mobile
Dermoscopic evaluation shows irregular red lacunae without septa and irregular linear vessels
Histopathology shows a well-circumscribed dermal vascular tumor
The tumor extends to the superficial subcutaneous tissue
The tumor is composed of ectatic thin-walled vessels with multiple intravascular branching papillary structures
The structures are covered by swollen endothelial cells with numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules
PAS staining shows positive hyaline globules in the cytoplasm of endothelial cells
Tumor vessels are positive for CD-31 and negative for D2-40 and HHV-8

shortlist.label: Hobnail Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches dermoscopic and histopathological findings of a vascular tumor with irregular red lacunae and ectatic thin-walled vessels

shortlist.label: Papillary Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similar histopathological features, including papillary structures and swollen endothelial cells

shortlist.label: Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Also known as Hobnail Hemangioma, this entity is a synonym and matches the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Pyogenic Granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, pyogenic granuloma can present as a vascular tumor and should be considered in the differential diagnosis

shortlist.label: Cherry Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: A common benign vascular tumor that could be considered, although the clinical and histopathological features are less consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of ectatic thin-walled vessels with multiple intravascular branching papillary structures, covered by swollen endothelial cells with numerous intracytoplasmic eosinophilic hyaline globules, and positive PAS staining are characteristic features of Hobnail Hemangioma.

rejected.label: Papillary Hemangioma
rejected.why: While it shares some features, the specific combination of histopathological findings and dermoscopic evaluation points more towards Hobnail Hemangioma.

rejected.label: Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma
rejected.why: This condition often presents with a targetoid appearance and significant hemosiderin deposition, which is not highlighted in the provided case facts.

rejected.label: Pyogenic Granuloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more rapid growth rate and is often associated with trauma or infection, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Cherry Hemangioma
rejected.why: Cherry hemangiomas are small, bright red, and usually have a different dermoscopic and histopathological appearance than what is described.
